findings.message: The new FORCE_COLOR behavior is not covered by any test. tests/test_colorama.py already has test_honor_no_color_standard (line 166) for the analogous NO_COLOR path, but no equivalent test exercises FORCE_COLOR (e.g. forced true with an isatty()==False stream, and the empty-string/NO_COLOR-precedence cases). As a result the new code path is unverified and the precedence semantics (NO_COLOR wins over FORCE_COLOR) are not locked in. This is a coverage gap, not a regression.
findings.suggestion: Add a parametrized test (mirroring test_honor_no_color_standard) asserting should_colorize(StreamIsattyFalse()) is True when FORCE_COLOR is set to a non-empty value, is False (fall-through) when FORCE_COLOR='', and is False when both FORCE_COLOR and NO_COLOR are non-empty.

findings.message: The new FORCE_COLOR support is user-visible but not documented. The CHANGELOG has an entry for the sibling NO_COLOR feature ('Honor the NO_COLOR environment variable...'), and docs/resources/troubleshooting.rst mentions NO_COLOR, yet no entry/addendum was added for FORCE_COLOR, so users have no way to discover the feature.
findings.suggestion: Add a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased (e.g. 'Honor the FORCE_COLOR environment variable to force color output by default if colorize is not provided') and mention FORCE_COLOR alongside NO_COLOR in docs/resources/troubleshooting.rst.

findings.message: The NO_COLOR check was changed from `"NO_COLOR" in os.environ` to `os.getenv("NO_COLOR")`. This is spec-correct (no-color.org requires a non-empty value) and does not break any existing test (test_honor_no_color_standard uses NO_COLOR='1'), but it is a behavior change bundled into a FORCE_COLOR feature: previously an empty `NO_COLOR=` disabled color, now it no longer does. Worth calling out explicitly as intentional since it changes prior released behavior.
findings.suggestion: Keep the change (it matches the no-color.org spec), but confirm it is intentional and note it in the CHANGELOG so users relying on `NO_COLOR=` (empty) are not surprised.
